# A Steampunk First: ‘A Master of Djinn’ Wins Nebula Award for Best Novel

Staff Report

May 26, 2022

A Master of Djinn Nebula

Congratulations to author P. Djèlí Clark, whose novel _A Master of Djinn_ received a Nebula Award on May 21 from the Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers of America (SFWA). It’s the first steampunk work ever to take the top honor in the novel category. The awards were presented during a ceremony at the virtual 2022 SFWA Nebula Conference.

The story takes place in the same alternate-world, early 20th century Cairo that was the setting for Clark’s 2016 novelette “A Dead Djinn in Cairo” and his 2019 novella _The Haunting of Tram Car 015_ .
In this reality, agents of the Ministry of Alchemy, Enchantments and Supernatural Entities contend with magical forces unleashed 40 years earlier by a Soudanese mystic named al-Jahiz.

The Nebula is considered one of the most prestigious awards in science fiction and fantasy, alongside the Hugo Award. _A Master of Djinn_ is also a finalist for best novel in this year’s Hugos, which will be presented at the World Science Fiction Convention in Chicago over Labor Day weekend.

_A Master of Djinn_ is Clark’s first full-length novel, but his shorter works have also received honors. _The Haunting of Tram Car 015_ was a finalist for the 2020 Hugo, Nebula, and Locus awards. And Clark’s 2020 novella _Ring Shout_ won a Nebula Award last year along with a Locus Award and British Fantasy Award. His 2018 short story “The Secret Lives of the Nine Negro Teeth of George Washington” won the Hugo and Nebula.
In brief acceptance remarks on Saturday, Clark expressed surprise at receiving the Nebula and credited his readers as inspirations for the novel. “When I first started writing in this world, I didn’t have any clear intention of writing a novel,” he said. But positive response to the novelette led him to write the novella, “and readers liked that, too.”

You can watch the entire [awards ceremony on YouTube](https://youtu.be/21VKlslZIRo) . The novel presentation is near the end, at 1:33.

Other Nebula winners this year included _And What Can We Offer You Tonight_ by Premee Mohamed (novella); “O2 Arena” by Oghenechovwe Donald Ekpeki (novelette), “Where Oaken Hearts Do Gather” by Sarah Pinsker (short story); and _WandaVision_ from Marvel Studios (dramatic presentation).

See the complete list of winners on the [Nebula Awards website](https://nebulas.sfwa.org/sfwa-announces-the-winners-of-the-57th-annual-nebula-awards/) .
For more info about _A Master of Djinn_ , see the [Macmillan Publishers website](https://us.macmillan.com/books/9781250267689) .

The **Nebula Award for Best Novel** is given each year by the [Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_Fiction_and_Fantasy_Writers_Association "Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association") (SFWA) for [science fiction](https://en.wikipedia.
org/wiki/Science_fiction "Science fiction") or [fantasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantasy "Fantasy") [novels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novel "Novel") . A work of fiction is considered a novel by the organization if it is 40,000 words or longer; awards are also given out for pieces of shorter lengths, in the categories of [short story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebula_Award_for_Best_Short_Story "Nebula Award for Best Short Story") , [novelette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebula_Award_for_Best_Novelette "Nebula Award for Best Novelette") , and [novella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebula_Award_for_Best_Novella "Nebula Award for Best Novella") . To be eligible for [Nebula Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebula_Award "Nebula Award") consideration, a novel must have been published in English in the US. Works published in English elsewhere in the world are also eligible, provided they are released on either a website or in an electronic edition.

...

During the 61 nomination years, 209 authors have had works nominated, and 48 of these have won (including co-authors and ties). [Ursula K. Le Guin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ursula_K._Le_Guin "Ursula K. Le Guin") has received the most Nebula Awards for Best Novel, with four wins out of six nominations. [Joe Haldeman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Haldeman "Joe Haldeman") has received the next most: three awards out of four nominations, while nine other authors have each won twice. [Jack McDevitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_McDevitt "Jack McDevitt") has the most nominations at twelve (with one win), while [Poul Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poul_Anderson "Poul Anderson") and [Philip K. Dick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_K._Dick "Philip K. Dick") tie for having the most nominations without winning an award, at five each.

## What are the Nebula Awards?

The Nebula Awards are presented by the Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers of America, Inc. Since 1965, the Nebula Awards have been given each year for the best science fiction or fantasy novel, novella, novelette, and short story eligible for that year’s award. The Award for Best Script was added in 2000.

Winners are announced each June.
